summary.text: 从 pictures two people arranged one after the other, interpreted as one following the other. Early uses with the sense ‘from’ are also reported, but their relation to ‘follow’ is uncertain.

formation.text: Pictographic compound: two 人 figures depict people arranged one after another, expressing a following scene. Neither figure is a movement marker or a sound cue in 从.

components.text: The visible 人 is one of the two pictured people in the reported following scene. No distinct earlier form is established for this component.
The second 人 completes the pair of pictured people. Together they are interpreted as one person following another; this element has no independent sound role here.

history.text: The graph is reported in oracle-bone and bronze materials. The curated oracle-style and seal-style depictions retain two human figures; the seal-style form regularizes their arrangement. These forms illustrate the paired-person analysis without establishing a direct sequence between the individual depictions.
In the historical analysis of 從, 辵 is added as a movement-related element while 从 serves as the sound element. This is a different graph construction; 辵 is not part of current 从.

uncertainties.text: The two-person reading is an interpretation of the early graph. The exact earliest date of the graph and of its reported senses is unresolved.

The Han dictionary treats 从 and 從 as separate entries, while a later editorial analysis relates ‘heed/obey’ to ‘follow/accompany’ by extension. The evidence does not resolve this difference or give a complete chronology connecting the reported senses.

senses.period: dating unresolved; reported in oracle-bone and bronze materials
senses.text: The paired figures are interpreted as one person following another. This is the earliest meaning supported by the graph analysis, though the earliest dated occurrence is not fixed.

senses.period: oracle-bone uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Early uses are reported with ‘from’ senses, including examples glossed ‘from the west’ and ‘from the east’. Their timing relative to the ‘follow’ use is unclear.

senses.period: Han dictionary account; earlier chronology unresolved
senses.text: The Han dictionary glosses 从 as ‘heed’ and analyzes it as two 人. A later editorial account relates this sense to ‘follow/accompany’ by extension, but the transition is not securely dated.

senses.period: bronze uses reported; exact dates unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples are reported for 从 meaning ‘follow’ and 從 meaning ‘accompany’. Their sequence relative to the other reported senses is not established.

senses.gloss: indulge (written with 從 as a loan for 縱)
senses.period: bronze use reported; exact date unresolved
senses.text: A bronze use of 從 is reported as a spelling for 縱 ‘indulge’. In this account, the graph was reused to write another word; ‘indulge’ is not a meaning shown to have developed from ‘follow’. The source word’s sound comparison and the borrowing’s date are not established.
These are supplied modern glosses. Their individual histories and development from earlier uses are not established.

developments.text: A later editorial account relates ‘follow/accompany’ and ‘heed/obey’ by extension, while the Han dictionary treats 从 and 從 separately. The evidence does not settle this development.
Both uses are reported for early material, but no dated sequence shows that ‘from’ developed from ‘follow’.

limitations.text: The reported uses do not establish a secure chronology or a complete semantic chain. Modern glosses alone cannot show how ‘from’, ‘since’, ‘through’, or ‘by’ arose.
No source word and sound match for a graph-loan account involving 从 or 從 is established here. Tentative proposed comparisons remain unverified.

items.caption: Two 人 figures are arranged one behind the other, a configuration interpreted as depicting following.
items.alt: Two tall, curved human-like forms stand side by side, each with a head-like top and a long descending body.
items.selection_reason: The visible paired figures support the reported two-person analysis and explain the ‘follow’ interpretation of 从.

items.caption: The seal-style form retains two 人 figures, regularized into a more even, upright arrangement.
items.alt: Two upright, narrow human-like forms with curved strokes stand side by side.
items.selection_reason: Shows the paired-person structure in the seal-script tradition; it complements the oracle-style candidate without asserting a direct sequence between individual forms.
